text:
maya: Quick rundown from the bench runs this morning — trying to size Dedicated pools for customer-X workload across us-west1 and eu-west1. Attached CSV + perf plots in the drive link. TL;DR questions below.
liam: link? can you paste the p50/p95 numbers here
maya: sure. us-west1 H100 80GB: p50=45ms, p95=120ms at 8k tokens/s aggregate. A100 80GB: p50=70ms, p95=200ms at same offered load. eu-west1 H100: p50=50ms, p95=140ms (higher network variance). Quantized int8 H100 (GPT2-style eval) dropped p95 to 110ms but some quality drift on long prompts.
sophia: nice, what was concurrency per GPU in the tests?
maya: concurrency target = 16 streams/GPU for H100 (we measured stable KV cache sizing). For A100 we could push to ~12 streams/GPU before lat spikes. Throughput per GPU (H100) ~ 480 tokens/sec at the 16-concurrency point.
jordan: what's the model? seq len / batch makeup?
maya: model=v3-13b-open (decoder-only). typical seq len = 1024, 25% of requests are >2k tokens. we trimmed evals to 1k for baseline but included long-tail tests.
ashley: any kernel differences? flash-attn vs cuDNN vs TRITON fused?
maya: flashed kernels (FlashAttention2) used on H100, TRITON fallback on A100 for some ops. We saw ~15-20% overhead when TRITON kernels used on A100 for the attention path.
liam: For Dedicated sizing: what's target SLO? 99th <= 250ms?
maya: customer wants p95<180ms, p99<350ms. We're aiming to reserve headroom for spikes and canary rollouts.
sophia: Ops rule of thumb: pick GPU_count = ceil(peak_offered_tokens / per_gpu_tokens_at_target_util) and then +20% headroom. For H100 numbers above, if peak_offered_tokens=120k tokens/s -> per_gpu ~480 -> need 250 GPUs -> +20% => 300 GPUs. does that match your calc?
maya: yes roughly. but we also want to maintain concurrency floor to avoid memory fragmentation. So autoscale config would be min_gpus=48, target_concurrency=14, scale_step=8, max_gpus=320 in region.
jordan: what about regional differences? eu-west1 had latency tail from NVSwitch contention and occasional PCIe fallback when noisy neighbors. I'd bias capacity +10% in eu-west1 compared to us-west1 for same SLO.
ashley: quantization quality issues — can we route long prompts to fp16 models and short ones to int8? that reduces capacity needs but complicates routing.
liam: yes, smart routing policy: if tokens_in_request > 1500 -> route to fp16 pool. Also we can cache common prefixes to reduce effective tokens for hot routes.
maya: proposed autoscale yaml snippet:
```
pool: dedicated-v3-13b-h100
min_gpus: 48
max_gpus: 320
target_concurrency: 14
scale_step: 8
headroom_percent: 20
routing:
  long_prompt_threshold: 1500
  fallback_pool: dedicated-v3-13b-fp16
```
liam: looks good. add a canary reservation (2% of pool) so rollouts don't saturate.
sophia: also add kernel_preference: ["flash_attention2","triton_fused","cudnn"] so scheduler prefers fastest available
maya: noted. action items: 1) finalize headroom calc and publish per-region capacity table 2) add routing rule for long prompts 3) run overnight stress with synthetic long-tail 4) confirm cost estimates for commit tiers. I'll open a follow-up doc.
infra-bot: deploy plan created: deploy/bench-dedicated-1753058400 (staging) — watchers: @eng-platform @eng-runtime
liam: thanks — ping me when the stress run finishes, I'll validate autoscale alarms. :thumbsup:
